name: Need for Cognition Scale, 6 item
domain: Self talk, thinking patterns and personality
developer: Coelho, Hanel and Wolf (2020); parent 18 item scale by Cacioppo, Petty and Kao (1984)
construct: Tendency to engage in and enjoy effortful thinking.
licence: Development paper (Assessment, 2020) is open access under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence (CC BY 4.0), copyright © The Author(s) 2018. PsyToolkit notes the scale may be used for research and that users "need to acknowledge the authors and their research paper when writing about it."
instructions: For each sentence below, please select how uncharacteristic or characteristic (5-point scale) this is for you personally.

items.text: I would prefer complex to simple problems.
I like to have the responsibility of handling a situation that requires a lot of thinking.
Thinking is not my idea of fun.
I would rather do something that requires little thought than something that is sure to challenge my thinking abilities.
I really enjoy a task that involves coming up with new solutions to problems.
I would prefer a task that is intellectual, difficult, and important to one that is somewhat important but does not require much thought.

scoring: Reverse score items 3 and 4 (1 = 5, 2 = 4, 3 = 3, 4 = 2, 5 = 1), then take the mean of the 6 items (1 to 5); higher scores indicate a greater need for cognition. PsyToolkit: "The score can range from 1 (you do not like deep thinking) to 5 (you like effortful thinking)." Reported sample means around 3.6 in UK and US samples (Coelho et al., 2020). No cut offs.
citation: Coelho, G. L. de H., Hanel, P. H. P., & Wolf, L. J. (2020). The very efficient assessment of need for cognition: Developing a six-item version. Assessment, 27(8), 1870–1885. https://doi.org/10.1177/1073191118793208
transcriptionNote: Items transcribed from the PsyToolkit survey library page and checked against the Appendix of the Sage article; wording was identical in both. Item 6 was returned in 2 segments by the fetch tool and is joined here. Only the endpoint labels are given in either source (PsyToolkit prints the middle points as dots; the article gives 1 = extremely uncharacteristic of me, 5 = extremely characteristic of me), so points 2 to 4 are unlabelled. The PubMed Central copy (licenceUrl in the target record) could not be fetched because of a browser check, so the Sage page was used for the licence. Page numbers 1870–1885 in the citation were not visible on the Sage page and should be verified.
